claims.text: Lightweight high-entropy alloys can combine low density with mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
This combination of properties is caused by a stable, refined grain structure and a homogeneous distribution of elements.
A stable, refined grain structure and homogeneous elemental distribution enhance grain-boundary strengthening.
A stable, refined grain structure and homogeneous elemental distribution reduce the formation of detrimental phases.
Hot rolling or forging followed by heat treatment will control grain size and morphology, elemental distribution, and phase composition.
Grain-boundary strengthening contributes to the alloy's mechanical response.
Solid-solution strengthening contributes to the alloy's mechanical response.
Precipitation hardening contributes to the alloy's mechanical response.
After equivalent processing, the high-entropy alloy will have greater mechanical strength than the conventional low-entropy baseline alloy.
After equivalent processing, the high-entropy alloy will have greater corrosion resistance than the conventional low-entropy baseline alloy.
After equivalent processing, the high-entropy alloy will have greater high-temperature oxidation resistance than the conventional low-entropy baseline alloy.
The proposed property combination should cease to hold above 1200°C.
The proposed property combination should cease to hold at high strain rates.
The proposed property combination should cease to hold in corrosive environments that accelerate degradation.
